submission.justification:
Sensor-T3 (planar sensor, standard pitch) at 185 µm thickness is recommended for the innermost pixel layer. This configuration achieves the best single-hit spatial resolution (9.033 µm) among technologies that meet the radiation hardness requirement. 

While Sensor-T1 offers superior resolution (6.0 µm at 150 µm), it fails the radiation hardness requirement with only 82% hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm² irradiation, well below the required 97%. Sensor-T2 (3D-electrode) exceeds radiation requirements (99.2% efficiency) but delivers significantly worse resolution (~14 µm at best). 

Sensor-T3 strikes the optimal balance: it comfortably meets the radiation hardness requirement (98.5% efficiency) while delivering 35% better resolution than Sensor-T2. The 185 µm thickness was determined through systematic simulation optimization across the 50-300 µm range, identifying the minimum resolution point for this technology.

requirements.requirement: The sensor must be one of the three technologies listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T3 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as 'planar sensor, standard pitch' and is qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip.

requirements.requirement: The sensor must be suitable for the radiation environment of the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T3 achieved 98.5% hit efficiency after irradiation to 2e16 neq/cm², exceeding the ≥97% requirement stated in irradiation_testbeam_2026.md. This confirms radiation hardness suitable for end-of-life operation.
The recommended thickness of 185 µm falls within the specified 50-300 µm range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Among radiation-hard technologies (Sensor-T2 and Sensor-T3), the recommended Sensor-T3 at 185 µm achieves 9.033 µm resolution, significantly better than Sensor-T2's best resolution of 14.041 µm. Sensor-T1, while offering better resolution, is excluded due to radiation hardness failure.
